III D network is a GCNN over the full space group with spin parity (App. F.4), whose group convolutions apply every kernel at each of the |G| group elements, as the model's GCNN entry does; the rectangular 4x8 torus has 4 point-group elements (Loehr & Clark count the same 4 for 4x16). The 'HFPS' ARCH entry's reuse = N is the CNN rows' value and undercounts this row 8x (verify/VERIFY.md Part 2, agent-C.md §4: implied 9.1 / 34 TFLOP/s instead of 1.35 / 5.1). The exact GCNN is not described (parameters 'roughly 600K'), so the reuse assumes a standard group convolution. proposals_per_sample absent: the sampler is not stated (Quantax's default sweep would be 4N if defaults were used, agent-C.md G2). The Pfaffian projection sums (32 on 16x4) run by low-rank updates and are <= 5 % of the forward (agent-C.md).

compute.reported_as: Supplemental Material Sec. 2 (Stochastic reconfiguration): where N_MC is the number of Monte Carlo samples, which is about 16000 in our calculations. Note O_p(s) can be stored trivially on different CPU processors, while still being convenient to iteratively solve the equation. In practice, we add a small diagonal regularization (e.g., ϵ = 10^−3) to S to ensure numerical stability. ... where dτ is the step size, which can be tuned from dτ = 0.1 to 0.01. ... Sec. 3: The neural network introduces variational parameters from the two fully connected layers, totaling approximately 4 N_neuron N + 2 N_det N_neuron M (including both weights and biases). The HB part contributes z d 2K M N parameters. Hence, the total number of variational parameters in the RHB wavefunction scales as O(N_neuron N) + O(N_neuron M) + O(MN). In this work, we typically set N_neuron = 100 and N_det = 5 (see later). ... Table III text: Increasing N_det to 16 (with N_neuron = 80) further reduces the error to 1.1 × 10^−3, but at a higher computational cost. Based on this tradeoff, we adopt N_det = 5 and N_neuron = 100 for all subsequent large-scale simulations. ... Acknowledgment: The computational resources utilized in this work were supported by SCNet Supercomputing Network.
